messages:
lia: Quick sync about rollout metadata for tenant-aware eviction/backpressure. We keep seeing reactive client storms when a model pin drops and clients immediately retry. Need a compact contract so routers, controllers, and SDKs behave consistently.
omar: Goal: minimal schema change, clear runtime semantics, and graceful migration for old clients. Sketching fields.
becky: Thumbs up. Also include guidance for operators so we don't silently degrade SLAs.
lia: Proposed minimal schema additions on the rollout object: `rollout_status`, `evict_phase`, `evict_window_ms`, `backoff_ms`, `fallback_candidate`, `quality_tier`, `tenant_slack_multiplier`, `reconcile_after_ms`.
omar: Definitions: `rollout_status` = active|degraded|evicted; `evict_phase` = none|soft|hard; `evict_window_ms` = how long soft serves before escalation; `backoff_ms` = router recommended Retry-After; `fallback_candidate` = model id or alias; `quality_tier` = high|medium|low; `tenant_slack_multiplier` = numeric factor to extend window per tenant; `reconcile_after_ms` = operator hint for reconciliation job.
controller-bot: note: controller v2 toggles `evict_phase` semantics (soft now allows limited TPS, not full pass-through). Flag `controller_sem_ver:2` will be added to rollout metadata during migration.
becky: Client contract proposal: Routers set HTTP 429 + header `X-Redwood-Rollout: soft` and `Retry-After` value in seconds computed from `backoff_ms`. If `evict_phase=hard` routers return 503 with `X-Redwood-Rollout: hard`. SDKs should implement exponential backoff capped by `allowed_retries` pref from rollout metadata or tenant default.
lia: Example header semantics (pseudo):

```
X-Redwood-Rollout: soft
Retry-After: 0.2
X-Redwood-Rollout-Fallback: model-compat-v2
```
lia: Note: Retry-After fractional seconds OK for SDKs; for raw HTTP clients map to nearest integer second.
omar: Important: `fallback_candidate` must carry a `compat_score` and `quality_tier`. If compat_score < threshold and tenant has `require_quality_gate=true` we must not automatic-fallback; router responds with structured warning and `allow_fail_open=false`.
becky: Add `allow_fail_open` and `quality_degradation_note` to rollout metadata as optional fields.
lia: Ops playbook: reconciliation job scans all rollouts where `evict_phase=soft` and created_at + `2*evict_window_ms` < now -> escalate to oncall channel. Also emit event `rollout.eviction.stale` with tags (tenant, model, controller_version).
devops: We'll add tracing spans: `eviction_decision` and attach `rollout_id` and `evict_phase` to traces. That helps perf analysis when retries spike.
omar: Migration plan: 1) Add new fields as optional with defaults (evict_phase=none, evict_window_ms=0). 2) Deploy controller toggled off by default. 3) Rollout sample tenants to verify SDKs and routers. 4) Flip default on after 2 weeks. Document in SDK changelog for unknown headers to be ignored.
becky: Security note: `fallback_candidate` IDs are tenant-visible; ensure we scrub internal-only aliases or tokenized IDs in metadata exposed to tenants.
lia: UX: Console should show `evict_phase` timeline and link to reconcile job. Also surface `quality_degradation_note` so CSMs can proactively reach customers.
devops: Quick implementation checklist: router header wiring, controller flag + schema migration, reconcile job (k8s cron), telemetry events, SDK backoff hook update.
omar: I'll draft a short RFC with exact schema example and a couple of flow diagrams (soft -> backfill success vs soft -> stale -> hard).
becky: I'll open the controller PR and include migration test harness.
lia: If no objections we'll run a 20min sync tomorrow to assign owners.
omar: sounds good.
lia: :rocket:
controller-bot: reminder: feature-flag created: rollout-evict-v2 (off).
devops: meeting: ops sync scheduled 11:00 UTC tomorrow.
